name: Cash Flow
tagline: Have I made more than I've spent?
subtitle: One question, answered honestly
pitch: Cash Flow syncs your accounts and answers the only budgeting question most people have. No categories to babysit, no envelopes, no guilt.
privacy: No analytics. No app backend. Your data stays on your phone.
status: Open source. Build it yourself from GitHub

features.title: The answer, up front
features.text: Net cash flow for any range, with money in and money out beside it. Press and drag the chart to see any day.

features.title: Your banks, without Plaid
features.text: Accounts sync through SimpleFIN. Or explore with demo data before you connect anything.

features.title: On-device AI that tidies up
features.text: Apple's on-device model cleans up merchant names and suggests categories. Tell the assistant a rule in plain language, preview it, and undo it if you change your mind.

features.title: Tags for real life
features.text: Tag spending the way you think about it, like “Japan Trip” or “Local Concert”, and see totals by tag.

features.title: Widgets and Live Activities
features.text: Net cash flow on your Home and Lock Screen across seven time frames, and progress in the Dynamic Island while a cleanup runs.

features.title: Locked by default
features.text: Face ID or Touch ID with a passcode fallback. Import and export CSV whenever you like.

engineering.intro: A small app with strict architecture: three modules, one composition root, and a CI check that fails the build if a layer imports something it shouldn't.

facts.v: uses of Double for money. Decimal throughout
servers. Everything runs on the phone

points.title: Clean Architecture that's enforced
points.text: The domain package imports only Foundation. A script in CI rejects SwiftData, ActivityKit or Foundation Models imports in the wrong layer, so the boundaries can't erode quietly.

points.title: Swift 6, complete concurrency checking
points.text: A single-flight sync coordinator and AsyncStream progress, all under strict concurrency.

points.title: Decisions written down
points.text: Architecture decision records cover SimpleFIN over Plaid, local-only SwiftData, the module boundary, and how category rules take precedence.

points.title: Foundation Models, on device
points.text: Title cleanup, category suggestions and natural-language rules run on Apple's on-device model. Nothing about your spending leaves the phone.

points.title: System integrations
points.text: WidgetKit with App Intents configuration, ActivityKit Live Activities, background processing tasks, Keychain and an App Group shared store.

try.title: Drag the chart.
try.text: This is the home screen idea in miniature: one number, one line, and your finger to ask about any day.
